Let \(p=\frac a4\). The line through the focus is
\[
y=m(x-p).
\]
Substitute into \(y^2=4px\):
\[
m^2(x-p)^2=4px.
\]
This quadratic has roots \(x_1,x_2\). Its sum and product are
\[
x_1+x_2=p\left(2+\frac4{m^2}\right)=8,
\]
\[
x_1x_2=p^2.
\]
Also,
\[
AB^2=(1+m^2)(x_1-x_2)^2=144.
\]
Since \((x_1-x_2)^2=8^2-4p^2=64-4p^2\),
\[
(1+m^2)(64-4p^2)=144.
\]
From the sum equation,
\[
p=\frac{4m^2}{m^2+2}.
\]
Let \(t=m^2\). Then
\[
(1+t)\left(64-\frac{64t^2}{(t+2)^2}\right)=144,
\]
\[
\frac{256(t+1)^2}{(t+2)^2}=144.
\]
Thus
\[
\frac{16(t+1)}{t+2}=12,
\]
so \(t=2\). Therefore
\[
p=\frac{4\cdot 2}{4}=2,
\]
and
\[
a=4p=8.
\]
\[
\boxed{8}
\]
